questions.question: Micro-economics is also called ________.
questions.solution:
The right answer is **__Theory of Price__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **theory of price**__ is a microeconomic principle that uses the concept of supply and demand to determine the appropriate price point for a good or service.
 
• This simple theory of determining prices is one of the core principles underlying economic theory.

questions.question: Transport comes under which sector of economic growth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tertiary sector.**__

__
 
• Transportation comes under the** tertiary sector.**__

__
 
• The tertiary sector or service sector is the third of the three economic sectors of the three-sector theory.
 
• The tertiary industry is one of three industry types in a developed economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• The primary sector includes the production of raw material and basic foods.
 
• The secondary sector of the economy manufactures finished 

 goods.
 
• The quaternary sector of the economy consists of intellectual activities.

questions.question: Which among the following refers to the existence of more than one level of Government in the Country?
questions.solution:
• Federalism is the mixed or compound mode of government, combining a general government with regional governments in a single political system.
 
• Examples of the federal government include the United States, Germany, Canada, Switzerland, Australia and India.

questions.question: Which among the following Amendment Act is also known as ‘Mini Constitution’?
questions.solution:
• The 42nd amendment to Constitution of India is known as Mini Constitution.
 
• It was enacted during the Emergency (25 June 1975 – 21 March 1977) by the Indian National Congress government headed by Indira Gandhi.
 
• It is most comprehensive amendment to the Constitution and carried out major changes.

questions.question: In which language did Vardhaman Mahavira taught?
questions.solution:

questions.question: During which period Non-Cooperation Movement gained momentum?
questions.solution:
• Non-cooperation movement was organized by Mahatma Gandhi, to induce the British government of India to grant self-government, or swaraj, to India.
 
• It was one of Gandhi's first organized acts of large-scale civil disobedience.

questions.question: The moon that we see in the sky is a ________.
questions.solution:
• The Moon is an astronomical body that orbits planet Earth.
 
• It is the Earth's only natural satellite.
 
• It is the fifth-largest natural satellite in the Solar System.

questions.question: The world’s longest river the Nile, flows through which continent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Africa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Nile is a major north-flowing river in north-eastern Africa and is commonly considered the longest river in the world.
 
• With a length of 6,853 km (4,258 miles), the Nile is an "international" river as its drainage basin covers 11 countries, namely, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Ethiopia, Eritrea, South Sudan, Republic of the Sudan and Egypt.
 
• In particular, the Nile is the primary water source of Egypt and Sudan.
 
• The river Nile has two major tributaries, the White Nile and the Blue Nile.
 
• The White Nile is considered to be the headwaters and primary stream of the Nile itself.
 
• The Blue Nile, however, is the source of most of the water and silt.

questions.question: Which category of compound is most concentrated energy source?
questions.solution:
__**Fat**__ is the most concentrated source of food energy.

 
• It is one of the three main macronutrients, along with carbohydrates and protein.
 
• Examples of fats are cholesterol, phospholipids.
 
• **Vitamin** is an organic molecule that is an essential micronutrient that an organism needs in small quantities for the proper functioning of its metabolism.
 
• **Protein** is a substance that has amino acids, compounds and carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen and sometimes sulfur and is found in many foods.
 
• **Starch** is a polymeric carbohydrate. This polysaccharide is produced by most green plants as energy storage.

questions.question: What is the main root of a plant known as?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The main root of a plant is called the taproot.**__
 
• The taproot system occurs in dicot plants and is one of the bases of distinguishing these plants from the monocots which have fibrous roots.
 
• In plants having a taproot system, the trunk-like primary root develops directly from the embryonic root called radicle and grows downward into the soil.

questions.question: The exchange of materials between blood and interstitial fluid occurs only at the _________.
questions.solution:
• The primary function of capillaries is the exchange of materials between the blood and tissue cells.
 
• Gas exchange occurs across capillary walls in a manner similar to that which occurs across alveoli and pulmonary capillaries.
 
• Substances pass through the capillary wall by ​diffusion, filtration, and osmosis.

 
 

 
 
Arteries

 
 
 
carry blood to all parts of the body from the heart

 
 
 

 
 
Veins

 
 
 
carry blood from different parts of our body to the heart

questions.question: The commonly used thermometric substance is ________.
questions.solution:
• Mercury is the only one in liquid state at room temperature.
 
• It is used in thermometers because it has high co-efficient of expansion.
 
• Hence, the slightest change in temperature is notable when it's used in a thermometer.

questions.question: Heat flows as a result of difference of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Temperature**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **

 
• Heat flows when you bring two objects of **different temperatures** together.
 
• Heat energy always transferred from the **hotter **to the **cooler **object.
 
• The objects will exchange heat until their temperatures are equal i.e. thermal equilibrium is reached.
 
• The temperature of a body can be defined as the state or condition which would determine the direction of flow of heat when this body is placed in contact with another body.

questions.question: A proton is identical to ________.

options.text: The nucleus of a hydrogen atom

questions.solution:
• A proton is identical to the nucleus of a hydrogen atom
 
• It is same as H+ (hydrogen cation) which means that if we remove all the electrons of Hydrogen then it will become a Hydrogen cation which is same as proton.

questions.question: An 𝛼 particle is ________.
questions.solution:
• Alpha particles consist of two protons and two neutrons bound together into a particle identical to a helium nucleus.
 
• An alpha particle is like Helium nucleus that and has no electrons and has the valency 2+.
 
• Alpha particles are emitted by radioactive nuclei such as uranium or radium, in a process known as alpha decay.

questions.question: What is the process of waste water treatment is commonly known?
questions.solution:
• Sewage treatment is the process of removing contaminants from wastewater, primarily from household sewage.
 
• Physical, chemical, and biological processes are used to remove contaminants and produce treated wastewater that is safer for the environment.

questions.question: Madhubani artwork started in which state of India?
questions.solution:
• Madhubani art also known as Mithila art is practiced in the Mithila region of Bihar.
 
• In this art form painting is done with fingers, twigs, brushes, nib-pens, and matchsticks, using natural dyes and pigments.
 
• The artwork is characterised by eye-catching geometrical patterns.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book named "Making India Awesome"?
questions.solution:
__
 
• 'Making India Awesome: New Essays and Columns' is written by **Chetan Bhagat__**.
 
• This book showers light on India's most obstinate snags-unemployment, violence, poverty, discrimination against women, religious fundamentalism, illiteracy and communal violence.
 
• It is a book of essays in which he analyses and provides inspired solutions to the country's most intractable problems.

questions.question: Which country has established new 2+2 ministerial dialogue with India similar to India Japan 2+2 dialogue?
questions.solution:
• India and US have established new two-by-two (2 by 2) ministerial dialogue to enhance strategic coordination between them and maintaining peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region.
 
• It will be similar to the India-Japan 2+2 dialogue format between foreign and defence secretaries of the two countries
 
• The 2+2 meetings have been held annually with the US leaders since 2018.
